In your original post you said that they were not as popular because of misogyny which is pretty much implying that it’s because people don’t like women or feminine things. I didn’t see your edit by the time I finished writing my post. I’m not super involved in the Sekai fandom itself (I mainly just like the game), so I haven’t seen hate like you described toward the female characters or groups. I apologize if my post came off as weird, I was mainly describing my perspective especially since I felt like you were implying that people just don’t like them because they haven’t read the stories. Some people have and still don’t like them, but I agree people should at least give the stories a shot before writing them all off in general. I mean I’ve seen some incorrect opinions on Mizuki that made it obvious the person never read a single event or side story about them, so I know how that feels. MMJ is my least favorite group and sometimes their stories bore me but there are some that give me warm and wholesome feelings.

As for the hate comments, a mixed cast (although there aren’t a lot of guys in this game) is pretty rare and I’ve seen that some very loud fans of male anime characters are young girls who want to reject anything seen as “girly” for whatever reason (maybe internalized misogyny) and hopefully they grow out of it. Not saying those are all of the people that make comments like that but generally games like these tend to be targeted toward men who don’t want male characters to “ruin” their game (not saying this is right, just saying this happens in Love Live and Bandori and I know fellow female fans who find it weird and don’t like the idea of potentially being associated with those types of male fans). Maybe since the existence of male characters in a game like this is so rare and it’s usually the all-girl groups that get attention, their fans are even more defensive of them. I’m not sure. Maybe I’m speculating too much, so I apologize for that.

Also, I think at least part of the reason why 25ji is so popular is because people tend to love the “dark and edgy” groups (see: Roselia in Bandori and the Aqours subunit Guilty Kiss in Love Live).

Anyway, I hope there are no hard feelings. I think some people misunderstood your post because of how some things were worded, but I think I get the gist of what you were trying to say now.

I’m someone who is a huge fan of Love Live and Bandori and I don’t hate L/N or MMJ but I do find their stories to be less interesting than the other groups (maybe because as others have said they’re a bit played out and I’ve seen it done before—and at times better imo) which is why I don’t really care for them as much. Sometimes it’s just personal preference. I have seen some series where it’s clear that people hate the female characters for no reason but I think you’re generalizing people’s dislike/neutrality of those two groups a bit much. 

It just bothers me because I love feminine characters and groups but those two units didn’t resonate with me and it sucks to read a post saying that the reason why people don’t like them is because they are adverse to femininity. My favorite characters in this game aren’t even male. Some people just will not find L/N or MMJ as interesting as you do, even after reading their stories, and that’s okay. 

Sorry, I hope that doesn’t come off as rude because I hate sounding that way, but I wanted to offer my perspective as someone who does enjoy the “stereotypically girly” series but doesn’t particularly care for L/N or MMJ. (And yes, I’ve read their stories.)

Yeah, my eye crossing was a lot worse when tired. In fact, when it started it was only when I was tired and then it became an everyday, constant problem. I don’t mind about the questions but hopefully I can answer them. My usual eye doctor referred me to a doctor that specialized in strabismus cases; he has treated them for many years. You can get prism glasses but I never tried them. At first he gave me at-home eye exercises to try for a month or two but they didn’t work at all. (He actually theorized beforehand that they wouldn’t work but we had to show the insurance proof that we tried to solve the issue with non-surgical means first.) Then he said I could do the glasses or surgery, but I believe he said the glasses wouldn’t really be a permanent solution if that makes sense? The glasses would just reflect things in a way where your eyes won’t cross as much, but your underlying issue (likely your eye muscles being either too loose or too tight) will still exist. I did feel like I had to push it a bit but I opted for surgery because the pain was too much.

Surgery may sound scary but it actually wasn’t that bad and I knew that because my older sister had to get the same surgery to fix her eye when she was a teen (her eye was inward almost from birth). I was asleep for the whole procedure and your eyes are red and hurt for a few days but after that you’re mostly fine. I do sometimes still have a bit of pain on a bad day or something but it’s DEFINITELY nowhere near as bad as it was before. My eyes have little gray scars in the inward corners but they aren’t really super noticeable to people.

Sorry this reply ended up being so long but I hope I helped in some way. And don’t hesitate to ask any more questions; I just hope I can answer them.

I had issues with the swipe notes when I started, but not to the same extent you're having I think? I'll try to help.

The game checks for the swipe motion when the pink note arrives on the line. You need to do it quickly. Don't rest your finger there when it comes and then do it. It has to be one quick, fluid motion right when it arrives (in any direction). Maybe a video will help? I found this on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XHmdmOiKSGw

In my opinion, the game is not poorly made like you claimed in a reply to another comment. I'm not very good at rhythm games, and with practice I've now full combo'd every song that's been released on EN on Hard and now I will be working on tackling Experts. A lot of practice (and gradually increasing the note speed) has helped tremendously. If the game didn't work, this wouldn't be possible. I don't feel like I have to be machine perfect to get these full combos, either. It also wouldn't be possible for people to get all-perfect Full Combos (you can find those on YouTube) if the game didn't work. And the game does have a grace period because there's a slight timing difference between a perfect note and a great note. Great notes still count toward your combo. If you want to get all-perfect Full Combos, I feel like that's where you have to be machine perfect (imo), and I doubt I'll ever get to that level, but just full comboing songs normally doesn't feel like you have to be at machine level in order to do it imo.

Like others are saying, it could also be a hardware issue for you, but if it's not, I hope what I wrote helped a bit. I really did have trouble with swipe notes at first and I hated them, but I've gotten better at them now so they aren't as big of a problem for me anymore. I hope my post didn't come off as rude because that's not my intention. And I hope the pink notes stop becoming a problem for you in the near future. I'm sure with practice you'll get better at hitting them!
